Pull request description:

  **Problem**: On Windows, `bitcoin.exe` spawns a child process and immediately exits rather than waiting for it to finish. This breaks capturing output and checking exit codes in scripts and tests.

  **Solution**: Switch `util::ExecVp` from `_execvp` to `_spawnvp(_P_WAIT)`, which blocks until the child exits and forwards its exit code. Also enable `tool_bitcoin.py` and `interface_gui.py` tests which were skipped due to previous behavior.

  This fix requires small changes to `src/util/exec.cpp` and `src/bitcoin.cpp` and there is also an extra commit fixing `errno` message strings on Windows when `ExecVp` fails. Details in commit messages.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36408: test: allow 3 bytes of fee overestimate in assert_fee_amount

050409b2c5522eff0dc37c00a6d1225a8a437e17 test: allow 3 bytes of fee overestimate in assert_fee_amount (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  The wallet sizes a transaction assuming a 71-byte low-R ECDSA signature. A signature whose r or s has leading zero bytes is shorter, so the fee can cover a few bytes more than the signed transaction needs. In #36394 the wallet estimated 219 bytes and paid 438 sat at 2 sat/vB, but the signed transaction was 216 bytes: the signature was 3 bytes short. That happens about once in 4 million signatures. `assert_fee_amount` allows only 2 bytes of overestimate, so the test failed.

  I raise the allowance to 3 bytes, which makes the failure about 200 times rarer. The check that the fee is not too low is unchanged. maflcko suggested 3 bytes in #24151 and #25164.

  Fixes #36394.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36757: net: ignore privacy network peer's view of our address

9cfd6014005197d9d2d67dacb3c079980e3b284c test: check privacy-network peers' view of our address is not used (stratospher)
533fee6b9da3801612f245af461fb2d8fb06f197 net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address (stratospher)

Pull request description:

  privacy networks set `addrMe` ("IP address peer thinks I am") in the VERSION message [as all zeroes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f103de70de0662a1395dca2e536cf5872d86eaa2/src/net_processing.cpp#L1667).
  this PR ensures we ignore it when processing VERSION message.

  this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions:
  1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman
  2. we need to be using a unique enough port. this would become easier in a future if we ever support random ports.

  h/t to Loupe and instagibbs for finding this fingerprint!

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36068: fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs

fd3b09e8bcb83351c30b37505501c2a9756d907e fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs (brunoerg)
2553b4cd9678f9d7ba78be3573eb3cd095ab3ea6 wallet: add test-only helper to clear in-memory transaction state (brunoerg)

Pull request description:

  FuzzedWallet was rebuilt for every input. That imports eight
  descriptors, and each address it then hands out costs a BIP32
  derivation plus three separate WalletBatch transactions (see
  DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetNewDestination) - all paid before the
  target reaches the code under test.

  This PR changes it to build the wallet once in the target's .init hook and
  reset it perinput instead. I benchmarked on my Ubuntu machine without
  sanitizers and got a ~6x speedup.

commit.message:
fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs

FuzzedWallet was rebuilt for every input. That imports eight
descriptors, and each address it then hands out costs a BIP32
derivation plus three separate WalletBatch transactions (see
DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetNewDestination) - all paid before the
target reaches the code under test.

Build the wallet once in the target's .init hook and reset it per
input instead.

wallet: add test-only helper to clear in-memory transaction state

Add CWallet::ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest(), which drops mapWallet,
wtxOrdered, mapTxSpends, m_txos and m_locked_coins, leaving the
database, the wallet flags and the ScriptPubKeyMans untouched.

This exists so that fuzz harnesses can reuse a single wallet across
inputs instead of rebuilding it for every one. m_txos and mapTxSpends
are private, so a harness cannot reset them on its own.

RemoveTxs() is not usable here: it erases each transaction's
m_it_wtxOrdered from wtxOrdered, and that iterator is only valid for
transactions added through AddToWallet(). Harnesses that populate
mapWallet directly leave it uninitialized.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36642: rpc: parse each batch element into its own request

5861dd29a73a9f0a21851a83adfa21d4637282b5 rpc: parse each batch element into its own request (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

  `ExecuteHTTPRPC` parses every element of a batch into the same request object, and `parse()` throws on a non-object before it sets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I give each element its own copy of the request, which holds only the HTTP fields, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.

commit.message: test: check privacy-network peers' view of our address is not used

net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address

- if i make an outbound connection to a tor/i2p peer
	me ---------> tor peer
  in the VERSION message the tor peer sends us back,
  there's a field which tells us about the address
  the peer thinks we are (addrMe) that can be used for
  self advertisement. Peers in privacy networks can't
  know this. So they send [::]:0.

  if a peer sends us a routable ipv4 address instead
  of [::]:0 - make sure to ignore it.

  if we don't ignore it, we can end up sending them
  as self advertisement the routable ipv4 address
  they sent us and our listening port. ignoring it
  will help prevent our custom clearnet port leaks
  to privacy networks.

scripted-diff: [fuzz] Add util/check.h includes for Assert

The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in
util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions.

So do that with a scripted-diff to use util/check.h.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-

 # Select all fuzz files
 paths=(
   'src/ipc/test/fuzz'
   'src/test/fuzz'
   'src/wallet/test/fuzz'
 )

 # Add the util/check.h includes
 for f in $(git grep -l --extended-regexp "\<(a|A)ssert\(" -- "${paths[@]}"); do
   if ! grep --quiet "util/check.h" "$f"; then
     line=$(grep --line-number --max-count=1 '^#include' "$f" | cut --delimiter=: --fields=1)
     sed --in-place "${line}i#include <util/check.h>" "$f"
   fi
 done

 # Remove cassert includes
 for f in $(git grep -l '<cassert>' -- "${paths[@]}"); do
   sed --in-place '/^#include <cassert>$/d' "$f"
 done

-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

rpc: parse each batch element into its own request

In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error
reply with the id and version of the element before it. A client that
matches replies by id can take that error for the result of the
previous call. If the previous element was a 2.0 notification, the
error is dropped.

Every element was parsed into the same JSONRPCRequest. I give each
element its own copy of the request before parsing, which holds only
the HTTP fields at that point. The functional test covers the two
cases.

  **Problem:** The IWYU CI job analyzes `src/ipc/libmultiprocess/` even though its results are thrown away.   **Problem:** The IWYU CI job analyzes `src/ipc/libmultiprocess/` even though its results are thrown away. Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36613: test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks

64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897 test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks (Aaron Leeb)

Pull request description:

  Add functional coverage for the `getblockfilter` error raised when a node has a known block header, but the block has never been connected.

  This gap in test coverage was identified by a coverage report generated while exploring BIP 157/158. The branch in `src/rpc/blockchain.cpp` was never executed in the measured tests:
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L3054-L3056

  The existing `getblockfilter` functional test checks unknown block hashes and filter retrieval for active and stale blocks, but doesn’t check a known header whose block has never been connected.

  This change submits only the block header of a newly mined block to a node using `submitheader` and verifies that in this expected state, `getblockfilter` returns error `-5` with `"Filter not found. Block was not connected to active chain."` This adds coverage for the RPC’s distinction between an unknown block and a known block for which no filter has been constructed.

  `rpc_getblockfilter.py` passes, and changing the error message makes the new assertion fail as expected.

40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 test: extract unknown fields passthrough to its own method (nebula-21)

Pull request description:

  I've tested some mutations related to test coverage for PSBT unknown field merging and discovered an inconsistency.
  <details>

  If line 71 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(psbt.unknown.begin(), psbt.unknown.end());`"  (inside `bool PartiallySignedTransaction::Merge(const PartiallySignedTransaction& psbt)` function) is removed then, the expected test fails: *"Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map."*

  If line 434 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(input.unknown.begin(), input.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTInput::Merge(const PSBTInput& input)` function), is removed, a different unexpected test fails: "*Test that unknown values are just passed through*".

  If line 537 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(output.unknown.begin(), output.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTOutput::Merge(const PSBTOutput& output)` function), is removed, the expected test fails: "*Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map.*".
  </details>

  This PR solves this inconsistency.
  The old code did 3 different things:
  1. Test the pass-through of unknown values for `walletprocesspsbt`.
  2. Combine two v0 PSBTs with different unknown input keys and check that both keys survive.
  3. Combine implicit v0 PSBT with explicit v0 and check that both keys survive.

  Case 2 is already fully covered by the existing `test_combinepsbt_preseves_unknown_fields` so keeping it is redundant and misleading.

  Commit 40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 moves the old code into a new method called `test_unknown_fields_passthrough` and commit ef4310097bd651497a98a9d1bb59560a7055ae01 removes the redundant code of Case 2 and moves Case 3 inside `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields`.

Pull request description:

  Most supported operating systems ship with clang-19 (or later), so bump the minimum to that and allow new code to drop workarounds for previous clang bugs.

  (For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)

  This patch will only be released in version 33.x, next year (2027).

  For reference:

  * https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/clang-22

  * Free/Open/Net*BSD ship clang-19
  * OpenSuse Tumbleweed ships with https://software.opensuse.org/package/clang (clang22); leap:latest with clang-19
  * macOS 14: depends/release cross-builds are unaffected and use clang-19
  * macOS 14: Native builds use llvm-19-ish via XCode CLT 26.3 since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36287
  * Windows: VS ships Clang 22

  On operating systems where the minimum Clang version is not shipped by default, the user would have to use GCC, or install Clang in a different way. For example:

  * https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/g++ (g++-12)
  * https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/g++-12
  * https://apt.llvm.org/, brew, nix, guix, or compile clang from source, ...

  `unsigned` is a 32-bit integer (even on 64-bit platforms). File sizes are generally measured in 64-bit integers and using 32-bit integers or architecture-dependent integers is brittle and confusing.

  So use u64 consistently for flatfile sizes in this refactor.

  Also, use `LARGE_INTEGER`'s `QuadPart` on Windows, which is recommended since C++11.

  Also, unit test VarInt overflow errors.

c000f6ef15e06856b9111ee433877a2b1bf31eb4 test: assert Murch-Zawy period boundaries (Sjors Provoost)

9f34ea1605bd0c8726cc69ecf5686cc6d3d0d125 test: rename REGTEST_RETARGET_PERIOD to HALVING_INTERVAL (Sjors Provoost)

Pull request description:

  This PR adds test coverage for what happens in the (extremely unlikely) event that the miner can't satisfy the constraints. This is inspired by the recently added timewarp-protection and Murch-Zawy rules (for the miner, not for consensus, see #30681 and #35949), but this is a pre-existing issue. It is not made worse by these rules.

  The test has an attacker mine 6 blocks, which set MTP at the victim's future-time limit. It calls `getblocktemplate` and the equivalent IPC method, which both fail. It then moves mock time one second forward, and demonstrates mining works again (and we don't drop the IPC connection).

  This (impractical) attack can be done at any height, be we illustrate it for blocks 142, 143 and 0 of a retarget period, to clarify that the timewarp-protection and Murch-Zawy rules do not matter.

  The test was added to `ipc_mining.py`, to avoid having to add IPC support to `mining_basic.py`. Mining coverage is currently split between various test files and not always mirrored between RPC and IPC. A followup could unify these, while still skipping the IPC side when that's not compiled.

  A few refactor commits to prepare:

  - fix incorrect name: `REGTEST_RETARGET_PERIOD` -> `HALVING_INTERVAL`
  - drop `REGTEST_` prefix from `REGTEST_N_BITS` and `REGTEST_TARGET` (consistent with `HALVING_INTERVAL`, `DIFFICULTY_ADJUSTMENT_INTERVAL` and `TIME_GENESIS_BLOCK`).
  - move `DIFFICULTY_ADJUSTMENT_INTERVAL` to the framework

  The last commit picks up a Murch-Zawy followup suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35949#discussion_r3944011135 and takes advantage of our refactor, but is otherwise unrelated.

Pull request description:

  The changes can be verified by running `test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh src/ipc/libmultiprocess` as described in [developer notes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/developer-notes.md#subtrees) and [lint instructions](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/tree/master/test/lint#git-subtree-checksh).

  Changes since last subtree update (#35720):

  - Adds support for nonunix platforms, making API changes that are not backwards compatible ([#274](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/274)). Follow-ups add a `CurrentThread()` accessor matching compatibility code in [bitcoin/bitcoin#35084](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35084) ([#323](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/323)) and remove code for Cap'n Proto versions before 0.9 ([#331](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/331)).
  - Fixes a data race between IPC calls running on worker threads and disconnects, found by Antithesis ([#349](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/349)).
  - Fixes a use-after-free when a socket disconnects before `ConnectStream` connects, and leaks and hangs when a client `construct()` call throws ([#298](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/298)).
  - Fixes a race where file descriptors from `SpawnProcess` could leak into processes forked at the same time by other threads, by clearing `FD_CLOEXEC` in the child after forking ([#311](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/311)).
  - Makes `SpawnProcess` report `exec` failures back to the parent and throw, reaping the child ([#312](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/312)).
  - Adds support for `std::chrono::time_point` fields ([#303](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/303)) and for serializing lists of interface objects that need to be moved from ([#304](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/304)), both needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#10102](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/10102).
  - Accepts container fields and parameters with any comparator, hash, and allocator types, like Bitcoin Core's `GCSFilter::ElementSet`, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#29409](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409) ([#379](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/379)).
  - Finds the `capnp` tool in vcpkg and Windows builds, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#32387](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32387) ([#317](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/317)).
  - Adds a `destroy_connection` option to `ServeStream` and `ConnectStream`, lets `ServeStream` take ownership of the init object and return the new server and its connection, and adds an `EventLoop::incomingConnections()` accessor, simplifying test setup in both repositories and needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#35932](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932) ([#365](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/365)).
  - Replaces `EventLoop::post()` with `sync()` taking a `kj::FunctionParam`, avoiding a heap allocation per call ([#347](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/347)).
  - Names threads spawned by the event loop so they can be told apart in tools and logs ([#324](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/324)).
  - Fixes warnings that Bitcoin Core enables or plans to enable: adds `[[noreturn]]` attributes for `-Wmissing-noreturn` ([#339](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/339), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#35911](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35911)), and fixes `-Wunused` ([#362](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/362), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36167](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36167)), `-Wunused-const-variable` and `-Wundef` ([#370](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/370)), and `-Wmissing-prototypes` ([#386](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/386), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36743](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36743)) warnings.
  - Fails at compile time with a suggested workaround when Cap'n Proto misdetects exception support (`KJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS`), as happens on NetBSD ([#364](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/364)).
  - Build improvements: fixes stale generated code when the `mpgen` binary changes ([#316](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/316)), fixes `mpgen` link order for static Cap'n Proto builds ([#367](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/367)), links `mpgen` against `kj-async` instead of `capnp-rpc` ([#327](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/327)), shows Cap'n Proto `find_package` diagnostics ([#325](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/325)), installs `type-unordered-set.h` and `version.h` ([#350](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/350)), and shows include-what-you-use errors instead of failing silently ([#371](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/371)).
  - Test, CI, documentation, and minor code improvements: fix for a startup race in the example program ([#315](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/315)), new test for immediate client disconnects in `ListenConnections` ([#310](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/310)), `ReadList` return value check ([#338](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/338)), connect test race fix ([#343](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/343)) and cleanups ([#344](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/344)), `std::ranges::copy` follow-ups ([#307](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/307)), trailing whitespace removal ([#345](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/345)), Cap'n Proto version documentation fix ([#357](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/357)), clang-tidy updates ([#358](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/358), [#360](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/360), [#380](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/380), [#389](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/389)), new CI job testing newer cmake and Cap'n Proto versions ([#212](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/212), [#359](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/359)), CI coverage for the minimum supported g++ ([#330](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/330), [#366](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/366)), new CI warnings ([#332](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/332), [#341](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/341)), CI parallelism ([#334](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/334), [#356](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/356)), CI diagnostics ([#351](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/351), [#352](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/352)), Nix and LLVM updates ([#296](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/296), [#363](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/363)), NetBSD and OpenBSD CI fixes ([#321](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/321), [#340](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/340), [#381](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/381)), building Cap'n Proto with GCC in the 32-bit CI job to avoid an ABI mismatch ([#383](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/383)), and GitHub Actions updates ([#387](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/387)).

  The second commit suppresses the clang `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` warning, which the new `[[noreturn]]` lambda attribute in `mp/proxy-types.h` triggers in C++20 builds. Since #31507 the Windows build uses clang-cl, so the same flag covers it.

  The third commit updates the minimum Cap'n Proto version in `doc/dependencies.md` to 0.9.2 (1.0 with Clang). This update raises libmultiprocess's own minimum from 0.7 to 0.9 (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#331), and libmultiprocess rejects 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 for CVE-2022-46149 and, with Clang 16 or newer, every version before 1.0.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36470: test: make p2p_eviction actually exercise block-time protection

2fd9be21e28fecf298493e28e90ccb8085aa4ae8 test: make p2p_eviction actually exercise block-time protection (Bruno Garcia)

Pull request description:

  `p2p_eviction.py` tests that 4 inbound peers that recently sent us a novel block are protected from eviction. However, the test currently passes even when that protection is not in effect.

  The block-sending peers are connected first, so they are the oldest connections. When block-time protection doesn't apply, `CompareNodeBlockTime` falls back to connection time and protects the 4 oldest peers, which are these same peers. Then the youngest remaining peer gets evicted. The check `evicted_peers[0] not in protected_peers` therefore holds whether or not block-time protection works.

  This can be shown by deleting the line where the peers send their block (L71 on master):
  ```py
  block_peer.send_blocks_and_test([block], node, success=True)
  ```
